To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mass wasting is a common process on convergent margins, and it is likely triggered by subducting topography.

(1) mass wasting processes are abundant in the continental slope offshore Costa Rica and Nicaragua; (2) the largest failures are triggered by collapse in the wake of large seamounts, but smaller features occur in response to the entire spectrum of topography of the underthrought plate; (3) the abundance of mass wasting features decreases from south to north; (4) the largest features offshore Costa Rica have detachment planes that penetrate the continental slope and reach the plate boundary; (5) the abundance
mass wasting processes in subducting margins are more abundant and important than previously recognized, and that they are strongly controlled by the tectonic setting.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how tectonic and sedimentary processes interact in the continental slope, and how they are affected by the presence of subducting plate relief.
the role of mass wasting processes on sediment dynamics and the role of subduction erosion in shaping the continental margin.
the processes that shape continental slopes and the implications of these processes for the evolution of continental margins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
subduction erosion is the dominant tectonic process in the region and that the continental margin is highly unstable.
subducting seafloor relief is a major preconditioning element for mass wasting in the continental slope.
subduction erosion and associated topographic relief on the downgoing plate is the main control on mass wasting processes in a convergent margin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
subduction erosion is the main process that controls mass wasting processes in this margin.
subducting oceanic plate topography is an important factor in the evolution of mass wasting processes along the convergent margin.
subduction erosion is an important process that can trigger mass wasting processes and affect the sedimentary record of the subducting plate and its overlying margin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mass wasting processes in subduction zones should be considered in models of sediment dynamics in convergent margins.
mass wasting processes are not only related to the presence/absence and type of gas hydrates but also to the intensity of subduction processes.
subduction erosion is an important process that affects the stability of the continental slope and the sedimentary record in convergent continental margins.
